source: Original CQA Chat Quality Checklist pp.1-3; user-relayed organizer clarifications O1-O7; case/CQA_SCORING_SPEC.md
rounding_note: Two decimal places are official. HALF_UP tie-breaking is a local reproducibility convention pending organizer clarification A06.

criteria.title: Establishing contact
criteria.instructions: The first human operator reply must greet the client in the client language AND introduce the operator. Bot greeting/introduction does not count. Do not invent a company script or timing SLA.

questions.question: Did the first human operator reply greet the client in the client language?
Did the first human operator reply introduce the operator?

criteria.title: Identifying the need
criteria.na_condition: Enough information to answer was available from the outset.
criteria.instructions: Consider details already known and clarify missing information before answering. Do not require redundant questions. N/A only if the stated condition holds.

questions.question: Was enough information available from the outset to answer?
If information was missing, did the operator consider known details and clarify the missing details before answering?

criteria.title: Identification
criteria.na_condition: The request did not require identification.
criteria.instructions: Confirm identity verification BEFORE disclosure of protected data or a protected action. For a general tariff question identification is not required. If a protected action requires verification and the transcript does not confirm it, answer no, not N/A. Do not assume invisible off-channel verification. Flag policy uncertainty for review.

questions.question: Did the request require identity verification before disclosure or a protected action?
If verification was required, is it confirmed before the protected disclosure/action?

criteria.title: Correct and complete consultation

anchors.0: No substantive answer, or the key recommendation is incorrect.
anchors.5: General guidance given, but the client still lacks a clear course of action.
anchors.10: Part addressed; a material question remains open.
anchors.15: Main question resolved; a secondary detail omitted.
anchors.20: All material questions are addressed, OR a correct next step is given.

criteria.na_condition: The conversation ended before the client formulated a request.
criteria.instructions: Map substantive customer questions to operator answers/next steps. Assess factual correctness and necessary next steps. Do not invent product policies; if correctness is unestablished, make the provisional anchor decision explicit and require review. N/A is not a substitute for factual uncertainty. A correct next step can earn full marks.

questions.question: Did the client formulate a request before the conversation ended?
Were all material questions addressed or a correct next step given?
Is the key advice factually correct on available evidence?
Were necessary next steps explained clearly enough to act?

criteria.title: Empathy and client orientation
criteria.instructions: The operator is polite AND, if the client expresses dissatisfaction or inconvenience, responds to that specific problem. Apply even if the client is not dissatisfied. No mandatory apology wording.

questions.question: Was the operator polite?
If the client expressed dissatisfaction or inconvenience, did the operator address that specific issue?

criteria.title: Dialogue management, speed and language quality

anchors.0: Incoherent or contradictory replies make the dialogue unclear.
anchors.4: Wording or response order forces the client to ask again.
anchors.7: One noticeable lapse, but the client can understand and continue.
anchors.10: Clear, coherent replies; warning given if there was explicit waiting.

criteria.instructions: Assess clarity, sequence and warning of explicit waiting separately from factual completeness in criterion 04. The three-minute first-response SLA, tags and attachments do not enter the score. Do not invent delay thresholds or spelling counts. For voice assess conversational logic, clarity, appropriate wording and pause management; do not infer acoustic tone/diction from text or penalize ASR spelling.

questions.question: Were the operator replies clear and coherent?
Did wording or order force the client to ask again?
If there was explicit waiting, did the operator warn the client?

criteria.title: Closing
criteria.na_condition: The conversation broke off before there was an opportunity to close it.
criteria.instructions: Working interpretation: (summary OR offer of further help) AND farewell. A routine operator closure without a farewell is no, not N/A. Cite evidence of interruption for N/A. Boolean scope remains an explicitly documented interpretation.

questions.question: Did the conversation break off before an opportunity to close?
Did the operator summarize or offer further help?
Did the operator say farewell?

criteria.title: Critical errors
criteria.instructions: Yes only for at least one of: insulting the client; offering a paid service bypassing the company; disclosing confidential information. A private paid offer itself suffices; acceptance/payment is unnecessary. Asking for a phone number alone does not establish the paid-private-service purpose. Missing identity verification alone is not proof of disclosure. For yes cite agent utterances and list categories; for no cite the complete inspected scope. No automatic numerical deduction.

questions.question: Did the operator insult the client?
Did the operator offer a paid service bypassing the company?
Did the operator disclose confidential information?
